# Draft:Ancient Warrior (Band)

----
}}
Ancient Warrior is a heavy metal music project founded in 1987 by musician Eric Austin. The project originated during the late 1980s as a band formed by four friends who shared an interest in traditional heavy metal and hard rock. In its early years the group performed cover versions of songs by influential rock and metal artists while also developing original material. Although several compositions were written during this period, the project became inactive in the early 1990s before those songs were formally recorded or released.
Decades later, Ancient Warrior was revived by its founding member as a studio based creative project focused on completing earlier compositions and producing new material. Many songs originally conceived during the project’s early years were revisited and developed into finished recordings, while additional material was written to expand the project’s catalogue. This revival approach has resulted in a body of work that combines ideas originating in the late 1980s with newly composed songs.
Musically, Ancient Warrior is rooted in the traditions of classic heavy metal, emphasising riff driven songwriting, slower and mid tempo structures, and atmospheric arrangements. The project draws influence from artists associated with the development of heavy metal and hard rock, including Black Sabbath, Whitesnake, Judas Priest, Guns N' Roses and Metallica. The project’s music typically features prominent guitar riffs, melodic vocal lines, and compositions that develop gradually through layered arrangements.
A defining characteristic of Ancient Warrior is its emphasis on narrative driven songwriting. Many songs explore themes such as mythological conflict, moral struggle, historical reflection, and psychological introspection. Releases are often conceived as concept driven works in which individual songs function as chapters within a broader narrative framework.
Since its revival, Ancient Warrior has released several studio albums including Sounds from My Psyche (2025), Tale of the Ancient Warrior (2026), Inhumanity (2026), and The Cross of Fate (2026). These works combine material originating during the project’s early creative period with new compositions written during the modern phase of the project.
History
Formation and early years (1987 to early 1990s)
Ancient Warrior was formed in 1987 by four friends who shared an interest in heavy metal and hard rock music during a period when the genre was undergoing significant stylistic development. The late 1980s represented a transitional moment in heavy metal, with traditional bands continuing to emphasise atmosphere and melodic structure while newer movements were introducing faster and more technically aggressive styles. Within this environment, the founders of Ancient Warrior gravitated toward the earlier traditions of riff driven heavy metal and blues influenced hard rock.
During its formative years the group focused primarily on learning and performing songs by established rock and metal acts. Rehearsals and early performances included material from influential bands such as Black Sabbath, Whitesnake, Judas Priest, Guns N' Roses, and Metallica. These performances were intended both as practice and as a means of understanding the structural elements that defined heavy metal songwriting, including riff construction, melodic development, and the relationship between rhythm and vocal phrasing.
The rehearsal process served as a practical education in the musical traditions that shaped the band’s emerging style. By studying and performing songs from established artists, the group developed an understanding of how guitar riffs, rhythm sections, and vocal melodies interacted to create a cohesive sound. Particular attention was given to the dramatic pacing and tonal atmosphere associated with earlier heavy metal recordings.
Alongside these cover performances, the band began developing original material. Early compositions were typically built around guitar riffs and lyrical concepts influenced by themes of mythology, conflict, and personal struggle. These songs reflected the band’s interest in storytelling and symbolic imagery, elements that would later become a defining characteristic of the Ancient Warrior project.
Although several songs were drafted and partially developed during this period, the band did not produce formal studio recordings or commercial releases at the time. As circumstances changed and members pursued different personal and professional paths, the project gradually became inactive in the early 1990s. Despite this inactivity, many of the ideas developed during these early years remained preserved in notebooks, rehearsal recordings, and unfinished song structures that would later contribute to the revival of the project decades later.
Dormancy and revival
Following its early period of activity in the late 1980s and early 1990s, Ancient Warrior entered a prolonged period of inactivity. As with many independent music projects of the era, changes in personal circumstances, professional commitments, and the practical challenges associated with maintaining a band led to the project gradually becoming dormant. Although rehearsals and songwriting had produced a number of early compositions, most of this material remained unfinished or unreleased.
Despite the project’s inactivity, the original ideas and compositions associated with Ancient Warrior were retained by its founding member. Song fragments, early lyric concepts, and partially developed arrangements continued to exist as part of the project’s creative foundation.
Decades later, Ancient Warrior was revived by founding member Eric Austin as a continuation of the original creative concept rather than a reunion of the original band lineup. The revived project operates primarily as a studio based endeavour, allowing material to be written, completed, and recorded without the logistical constraints associated with maintaining a traditional performing group.
A central aspect of the revival has been the revisiting of compositions originally written during the project’s early years. These songs are being reconstructed and completed with attention to preserving their original musical character while benefiting from modern recording and production techniques. This process involves developing early riffs, lyrical fragments, and structural ideas into fully realised compositions.
Alongside the restoration of earlier material, the revived project has also produced new songs that expand the thematic and musical scope of Ancient Warrior. These newer compositions maintain continuity with the project’s original stylistic influences while reflecting the experience and perspective gained over the intervening decades.
The modern incarnation of Ancient Warrior functions primarily as a creative studio project focused on songwriting, recording, and conceptual album development. This approach allows the project to maintain its emphasis on narrative driven heavy metal while continuing the creative vision originally established during its formation in 1987.
Musical style
Ancient Warrior’s musical style is rooted in traditional heavy metal and reflects the sound and compositional approach of heavy metal bands from the 1970s and 1980s. The project emphasises weight, atmosphere, and deliberate pacing rather than speed driven arrangements. Guitar riffs form the structural foundation of most compositions, supported by prominent bass lines and steady rhythmic patterns.
The music draws influence from early heavy metal pioneers such as Black Sabbath, particularly in the use of slow to mid tempo riff structures and darker tonal atmospheres. The dramatic melodic approach associated with Ronnie James Dio era heavy metal is also reflected in the project’s emphasis on soaring vocal lines and narrative lyric delivery.
Elements of classic British heavy metal are present in the sharper guitar arrangements and rhythmic precision reminiscent of Judas Priest. The project also incorporates melodic and dramatic influences from hard rock acts such as Whitesnake, particularly in the use of sweeping melodic passages and structured song dynamics.
Ancient Warrior’s compositions typically favour slower development and layered atmosphere. Riffs are often repeated and expanded to create tension and weight, allowing the music to build gradually rather than relying on rapid tempo changes. This approach reflects the stylistic traditions of early heavy metal where mood and sonic texture are central elements.
The project also incorporates elements commonly associated with epic and doom influenced heavy metal. Songs frequently feature darker tonalities, extended instrumental passages, and thematic arrangements designed to evoke a sense of scale and narrative progression.
Lyrically and structurally, Ancient Warrior emphasises storytelling. Songs are often written as narrative pieces built around symbolic imagery and historical or mythological themes. This narrative focus influences the pacing of the music, with arrangements structured to support the progression of the story rather than conforming strictly to conventional verse and chorus formats.
The overall style has been described as traditional heavy metal characterised by slow to mid tempo riff driven arrangements, melodic vocal passages, and narrative oriented songwriting rooted in the traditions of classic heavy metal music.
Themes and lyrical content
The lyrical themes explored by Ancient Warrior centre on narrative storytelling, frequently drawing upon historical imagery, mythology, and symbolic representations of conflict and endurance. Songs are often constructed as narrative chapters rather than isolated lyrical pieces, with recurring motifs that connect individual compositions across releases.
Many songs incorporate imagery associated with battle, loyalty, and sacrifice. These elements are often presented through symbolic language involving natural and elemental imagery such as stone, steel, fire, snow, and blood. Within the project’s lyrical framework, these motifs function as metaphors for resilience, struggle, and the passage of time rather than literal depictions of fantasy or warfare.
A recurring theme within the project’s writing is the concept of the fallen or enduring warrior. This figure is used symbolically to explore broader ideas about personal conviction, moral conflict, and the burdens associated with leadership or belief. The warrior archetype serves as a narrative device through which themes of loyalty, betrayal, faith, and perseverance are explored.
Ancient Warrior’s lyrics also frequently address the consequences of human decisions, particularly the ways in which belief systems, authority, and ideology shape historical events. Some compositions explore the darker aspects of human behaviour, including cruelty, corruption, and the erosion of moral boundaries. These themes are particularly present in concept driven works such as Inhumanity, which examines the destructive potential of human actions and the societal forces that enable them.
Mythological and historical inspiration also plays a role in the project’s lyrical approach. Certain works draw on classical mythology and ancient cultural narratives, using these traditions as a framework for exploring universal themes such as power, fate, and the relationship between individuals and larger historical forces. Planned projects such as Pantheon of the Damned expand this approach by focusing on figures from Greek mythology and interpreting their stories through a heavy metal narrative lens.
Across the project’s catalogue, the lyrical style emphasises atmosphere and symbolism rather than direct storytelling. The use of recurring imagery and thematic continuity allows individual songs to function as part of a broader narrative structure, with releases often conceived as chapters within a larger conceptual saga.
Songwriting approach
The songwriting approach used in Ancient Warrior is characterised by a deliberate and structured compositional process that places emphasis on atmosphere, pacing, and thematic cohesion. Rather than prioritising speed or technical complexity, the project focuses on developing musical ideas gradually, allowing riffs, melodies, and lyrical themes to evolve over the course of a composition.
Songs typically begin with a central guitar riff or thematic concept. This initial musical idea often establishes the tonal character and emotional direction of the piece. From this foundation, arrangements are developed through layered instrumentation, dynamic shifts, and melodic variation. The pacing of the music is intentionally measured, with riffs and motifs often repeated and expanded to reinforce mood and narrative tension.
The project frequently utilises slower and mid tempo structures that emphasise weight and sonic depth. This approach reflects the influence of traditional heavy metal songwriting where atmosphere and structural development play a central role in shaping the listening experience. Instrumental passages are commonly used to build momentum between vocal sections, allowing musical themes to develop before returning to lyrical storytelling.
Lyrical and musical composition are often developed simultaneously. Narrative themes frequently inform the structure of the music itself, with changes in tempo, harmony, or arrangement reflecting shifts within the story being told. In this way, the songwriting process aims to integrate musical and lyrical elements into a cohesive narrative framework.
Another aspect of the project’s approach involves revisiting and completing material originally written during the late 1980s. These earlier compositions are developed with an effort to preserve their original stylistic character while adapting them to contemporary recording and production techniques. This process allows unfinished ideas from the project’s early years to be incorporated into the modern catalogue.
New material continues to be written alongside these restored compositions, maintaining continuity with the project’s original musical vision while expanding its thematic scope. The result is a catalogue that combines historical ideas with newly developed material, unified by a consistent emphasis on narrative driven heavy metal songwriting.

Sounds from My Psyche (2025)
Sounds from My Psyche presents a more introspective direction for Ancient Warrior, drawing on darker psychological themes and internal conflict. The album explores the human mind, memory, and emotional turmoil through atmospheric heavy metal compositions.

Tale of the Ancient Warrior (1987-2026)
Tale of the Ancient Warrior is a concept album centred on themes of mythic struggle, destiny, and the endurance of warriors across time. The album reflects the narrative storytelling approach that defines much of Ancient Warrior’s music, with songs built around imagery of battle, loyalty, sacrifice, and fate. Much of the material originated during the project’s early creative period in the late 1980s before being completed and recorded decades later.

Whispers in the Gallows Wind (forthcoming)
Whispers in the Gallows Wind is an upcoming album by Ancient Warrior. The project continues the band’s focus on narrative heavy metal, incorporating themes of judgement, consequence, and endurance. The album is expected to feature slow to mid tempo riff driven compositions influenced by traditional heavy metal of the 1970s and 1980s.
